m1.name: widget.add
m1.summary: Add ONE widget of a given type to the Charts workspace, placed automatically in empty space. Use one op per widget.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. "as" NAMES THE NEW WIDGET: if any later op in this plan changes the new widget (a new chart's symbol, timeframe, …), set "as" to a short unique name (new1, new2, …) and use exactly that name as those ops' target — a later op may not target a new widget whose "as" is null. Otherwise "as" is null. Example: "add 2 charts on SPY and QQQ" → widget.add{type:chart, as:"new1"}, widget.add{type:chart, as:"new2"}, chart.setSymbol@new1{SPY}, chart.setSymbol@new2{QQQ}. Never drop a ticker the member named ("open a QQQ chart" needs its chart.setSymbol). Types: chart (Chart), watchlist (Watchlist), themes (Theme Tracker), scanner (Scanner), fundamentals (Fundamentals), breadth (Breadth), aisearch (AI Search), news (News & Catalysts), notebook (Notebook), profile (Stock Profile), alerts (Alerts), calendar (UCT Terminal), optionsflow (Options Flow), nhnl (New Highs / Lows), nhnlPulse (H/L Pulse), volumescan (Volume Surge), scatter (Market Map).

m1.name: widget.addCharts
m1.summary: Add one NEW chart per symbol of an ordered list (tickers, a screen's results, or a saved watchlist), placed together in empty space. Existing widgets are never changed.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the workspace entry. symbols = the tickers, uppercase, OR {from, top} to chart a source's stocks in its order: from = the ref of a saved watchlist (its stocks, read fresh in its saved order when they apply), the "as" of a screener.run / screener.runSaved op in this request, or "lastScreen" for the last screen run here; top = how many charts (required, at most 12). timeframe: 1|5|15|30|60 minutes, D, W, M, or null to keep the default. chart_type: candles|hollow|bars|hlc|line|area or null. exact: true only if they insist on exactly that many (else fewer results just make fewer charts). Use this — not widget.add + chart.setSymbol — whenever the charts' symbols come from a screen or watchlist. Never type tickers you have not been given.
m1.shape: {"symbols":["NVDA"],"timeframe":"D","chart_type":null,"exact":null} or {"symbols":{"from":"<watchlist ref or screen as>","top":2},"timeframe":null,"chart_type":null,"exact":null}; timeframe 1|5|15|30|60|D|W|M (D daily, W weekly, M monthly, 60 hourly). No other keys: indicators, a row or a position cannot be set here — plan the charts alone and say in `reply` that indicators can be added next. ⛔ With NO chart in <workspace_context>, "add / open / show a <timeframe> chart of <symbol>" is THIS op on the workspace entry — never chart.setSymbol / chart.setTimeframe on a chart that does not exist.

m1.name: screener.run
m1.summary: Run a stock screen on UCT's Screener and show the real matches (count + top rows). Changes nothing in UCT. Use this for "show me / find stocks with …".
m1.hints: target = the screener entry ref. Comparisons, OR/NOT, rank: `compose`. filters: each {field: a key from `fields` (never invented), op, value, max, values}. Numbers: op gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between, value, max (between only, else null), values null; % fields take 5 for 5%, $ fields take dollars (10M = 10000000). yes/no: op eq, value 1|0. (list) fields: op in|not_in, values = the member's own words (["software"]) — UCT matches real values; value/max null. "(latest session)" fields only when a session is named ("today", "yesterday"); "$10M a day" / "per day" if none named = the 30-day average, not share volume. A measure not in `fields`: say so, never substitute. sort_field/sort_dir or null. mode refine = change the LAST screen, else new. show: rows (null = 10, max 25). as: name the RESULT (screen1) when a later op uses its stocks ({from:"screen1", top:null} = all); else null. within: a watchlist ref only if they name that list ("in Momentum"); else null (whole market).
m1.shape: a refinement that only changes the ORDER ("sort them by 3-month performance") is {"filters":[],"sort_field":"chg_pct_3m","sort_dir":"desc","mode":"refine","show":null,"as":null,"within":null,"logic":null,"rank":null} — filters is ALWAYS present ([] when nothing is added), sort_field is a key from `fields`, sort_dir is exactly "asc" or "desc" (never "descending"), and there is no nested "sort" object.

m1.name: screener.runSaved
m1.summary: Run one of the member's saved screens (or a UCT starter screen) and show the real matches.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry; screen = the id of an entry in savedScreens (never invent one; clarify with the real names if unsure). show: rows (null = 10). as: name its RESULT when a later op in the same request uses its stocks; else null.

m1.name: screener.state
m1.summary: Say what the last screen run here was: its filters, sort and number of matches.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m1.name: screener.listSaved
m1.summary: List the member's saved screens and UCT's starter screens.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the screener entry.

m1.name: screener.saveAs
m1.summary: Save the LAST screen run here (its exact filters, sort, ranking and logic) as a new saved screen in the member's Screener. Never replaces an existing one.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; name = the name as given. It saves the last screen run here — one run earlier in this conversation, or earlier in this same request. To run a NEW screen and save it in one request: the screen first, then this — it saves that screen.

m1.name: screener.duplicateSaved
m1.summary: Copy a saved screen (one of the member's or a UCT starter) to a new saved screen with exactly the same definition (filters, sort, ranking, logic, view, columns).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of the screen to copy (from yours, or a starter id from the screener entry's savedScreens); name = the new name as given, or null for "<name> copy" (do not ask for a name).

m1.name: screener.renameSaved
m1.summary: Rename one of the member's own saved screens.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens; name = the new name as given.

m1.name: screener.deleteSaved
m1.summary: Delete one of the member's own saved screens (permanent). UCT's starter screens cannot be deleted.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the savedScreenLibrary entry; screen = the id of one of YOUR screens. If more than one could be meant, clarify with the real names — never pick one by similarity. Deleting is always shown as a proposal first, so do not ask "are you sure?".

m1.name: widget.remove
m1.summary: Remove a widget from the board (any type). Undo puts it back exactly — same place, size, link colour and settings. The space it leaves stays empty unless widget.arrange fills it.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of the widget from the board entry's widgets. If several could be meant, clarify — never guess.

m1.name: widget.move
m1.summary: Move and/or resize ONE widget to a rectangle on the board grid, exactly like dropping it there: the other widgets re-tile around it.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; x, y = the new top-left cell (columns from 0 at the left, rows from 0 at the top); w, h = the new width/height in cells, or null to keep the current size. The board entry gives the grid size and every widget's x/y/w/h. "to the left" = x 0; "narrower" = smaller w; "full height" = y 0 and h = rows.

m1.name: widget.arrange
m1.summary: Re-arrange widgets: "fill" grows them into the empty space around them (nothing else moves); "grid", "columns" or "rows" re-tile them evenly over the area they cover.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widgets = the ids to arrange, or null for every widget on the board; pattern = fill | grid | columns | rows. "make the remaining charts fill the space" = fill on those charts (after a widget.remove in the same plan).

m1.name: widget.setLink
m1.summary: Set a widget's link colour: widgets with the same colour follow the same symbol; N = not linked.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; color = A (gold), B (blue), C (green), D (purple), E (red), F (teal), G (orange), H (pink), N (not linked) — E–H only when the board entry says extraLinkColors: true. "Link these two charts" = give both the same colour (use one already on one of them).

m1.name: widget.showList
m1.summary: Make a Watchlist widget show one of the member's own watchlists (what picking it in the widget does).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a watchlist widget; list = the ref of the watchlist (from watchlists).

m1.name: widget.showScan
m1.summary: Make a Scanner widget show one of UCT's scans (what picking it in the widget does).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = the id of a scanner widget; scan = highest-volume-1y (Highest Volume In 1-Year), highest-volume-ever (Highest Volume Ever), ipo-1y (IPO in Last 1-Year), top-gainers-30d (Top Gainers (30-Day)), top-gainers-60d (Top Gainers (60-Day)), top-gainers-90d (Top Gainers (90-Day)).

m1.name: widget.resize
m1.summary: Resize ONE widget by moving one of its edges, exactly like dragging that edge: the widget the edge moves into shrinks (never below its minimum); nothing leaves the board.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; edge = left | right | top | bottom; by = cells to move the edge OUTWARD (positive = bigger, negative = smaller). "Make my watchlist narrower and give the chart more space" = resize the CHART toward the watchlist (the watchlist shrinks), or the watchlist inward then widget.arrange fill on the chart.

m1.name: widget.selectTab
m1.summary: Switch a widget to one of its tabs (clicking the tab in the widget header).
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab).

m1.name: widget.renameTab
m1.summary: Rename one of a widget's tabs (double-click the tab), or clear the name back to the automatic label. At most 24 characters.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab). name = the new name, or null to go back to the automatic label.

m1.name: widget.closeTab
m1.summary: Close one of a widget's extra tabs (its ×); the widget's own main tab cannot be closed. Undo puts the tab back exactly, settings included.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; tab = "main" (the widget's own content), "1", "2"… or the tab's name, from the board entry's widgetTabs. NOT chart tabs (those are chart.*Tab).

m1.name: widget.addTab
m1.summary: Add another widget as a TAB inside an existing (non-chart) widget — the widget header's "+" — and show it. Nothing else on the board moves. Undo closes it.
m1.hints: target = the ref of the board entry; widget = its id; type = one of chart, watchlist, themes, scanner, fundamentals, breadth, aisearch, news, notebook, profile, alerts, calendar, optionsflow, nhnl, nhnlPulse, volumescan, scatter. For a chart's own tabs (symbols, timeframes) use chart.addTab.

m1.name: indicator.list
m1.summary: List the indicators on ONE chart (as its legend names them): built-in or custom, shown or hidden, on the price chart or in its own pane. UCT answers from the chart's real state — use this (disposition apply) whenever they ask what indicators are on a chart, whether one is on, or which are hidden, instead of answering yourself.
m1.hints: target = the indicators entry for the chart the member means (with several charts and no chart named, ask which). filter: hidden | shown | null (all).

m1.name: indicator.add
m1.summary: Add ONE indicator to ONE chart — exactly what the Indicator Library's Add to Chart does. Built-in indicators or the member's own saved ones; Undo removes it again.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. defId = an id from indicatorCatalog (never invented, never a name). The SAME indicator on several charts = one indicator.add per chart named, same defId; if it isn't clear which charts, ask. Classic overlay averages (the legacy EMA/SMA rows) are NOT added this way — say they live in Chart Settings. Volume Profile: volumeProfile.set. inputs = null for the indicator's defaults, else [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that row's `settings` ("a 20 EMA" → movingAverage, [{key:"period",value:20},{key:"maType",value:"ema"}]; "RSI 7" → rsi, [{key:"period",value:7}]). Every number or type the member named goes in inputs — never drop one or add a default instead. A setting the row does not list: say it isn't available; never guess a key. A moving average named by its LENGTH only ("the 9 and 20", "a 50 ma"): EMA for 8, 9, 10, 20 and 21, SMA for 50 and above (the member's default — say which you used); any other length: ask EMA or SMA.

m1.name: indicator.remove
m1.summary: Remove ONE indicator (its whole group, e.g. all COT panes) from ONE chart — the settings ✕ / legend Delete. Always shown as a proposal first, listing anything it would disconnect. Undo restores it exactly (same identity, reconnected inputs).
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m1.name: indicator.update
m1.summary: Change the settings of ONE indicator already on ONE chart, in place — its length, its moving-average type, or another setting its row lists (what the indicator's settings dialog does). Never adds a second copy. Undo puts the old settings back.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). inputs = [{key, value}] with ONLY keys from that indicator's settings, and ONLY the settings the member named — everything else stays as it is (an EMA stays an EMA unless they name a type). "make it a 9" right after adding an EMA 20 → that EMA, [{key:"period",value:9}]; "change that to an SMA" → [{key:"maType",value:"sma"}]. Use this — never indicator.remove + indicator.add — to change an indicator that is already on the chart.

m1.name: indicator.show
m1.summary: Show ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m1.name: indicator.hide
m1.summary: Hide ONE indicator (its whole group) on ONE chart — the settings / legend eye. Undo puts it back.
m1.hints: target = the ref of that chart's indicatorEdits entry. instance = the indicator's `id` from that chart's indicators list (exact; a name only if it is unique). Volume is not an indicator (use volume.setState).

m2.name: breadth.show
m2.summary: MARKET BREADTH from UCT's own data (US, NYSE, Nasdaq): now, on a date or at the close (a close not finalized yet is labelled provisional), the last N sessions, two dates compared, or a range — % above a moving average, new highs/lows, advance/decline, Stage 2/4. UCT shows the figures; you never see them. Use this (disposition apply, research null), never state breadth figures yourself.
m2.hints: target = breadth ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct. metrics 1–4 keys; [] = general overview. value: date null = now; basis "close" if a close is asked; side "below" for % BELOW MA; else null. compare: compare_date. series: start, end null = latest. rows: sessions N = last N readings. Dates YYYY-MM-DD or null. reply: one short line, no figures. Keys: pct_above_{5,10,20,40,50,100,150,200}sma = % of stocks above that N-day simple MA; new_52w_highs/new_52w_lows = counts at 52-week highs/lows; net_new_high_low = highs minus lows; hi_ratio/lo_ratio = % of stocks at 52-week highs/lows; new_20d_highs/new_20d_lows = 20-day; near_52w_high = within 5% of 52w high; up_4pct_today/down_4pct_today = up/down 4%+ that day; ratio_5day/ratio_10day = up-4%/down-4% ratio over 5/10 days; adv_decline = net advancers; advancing/declining = issues up/down; universe_count = stocks counted; stage2_count/stage4_count = Stage 2 uptrend / Stage 4 downtrend counts.

m2.name: breadth.history
m2.summary: Search UCT's finalized daily MARKET BREADTH history (US, NYSE, Nasdaq) for when a condition held: the last/first time a measure was below/above a level, crossings, how many times, episodes and how long they lasted. UCT computes it and shows the member; you never see figures. Never say UCT lacks historical breadth.
m2.hints: target = breadth entry ref. universe us (default) | nyse | nasdaq | uct; metric = ONE key (same keys as breadth.show). op below | at_or_below | above | at_or_above (strict unless at_or) | crosses_below | crosses_above; level in the measure's unit (10 = 10%). find last | first (date of the most recent / earliest match) | count (sessions + episodes; crossings for crosses_*) | episodes | longest | last_episode (runs of consecutive sessions). start / end YYYY-MM-DD or null (all history). aggregation "daily". A follow-up "that" / "it" = the measure and universe of the member's last breadth request. Lowest / highest in a period: breadth.show mode series. reply: one short line, no figures.

m3.name: chart.setType
m3.summary: Change how price is drawn on one chart.

m3.name: chart.setTimeframe
m3.summary: Change one chart's timeframe.
m3.hints: 1/5/15/30/60 min, D, W, M; next/previous: one rung.

m3.name: chart.setSymbol
m3.summary: Show a different ticker on one chart. Widgets linked to the same color group follow, exactly as a manual symbol search does.

m3.name: chart.setSession
m3.summary: Show or hide pre/post-market (extended hours) on one chart.

m3.name: chart.setScale
m3.summary: Set one chart's price scale: linear (arithmetic), logarithmic, or percent.

m3.name: chart.applyTheme
m3.summary: Apply one of UCT's built-in chart color themes (canvas, candles, grid, text) to one chart.

m3.name: chart.setBackground
m3.summary: Set one chart's background to a single solid color.
m3.hints: Pass a hex color like #f3efe4; translate plain color names to hex.

m3.name: chart.setCandleColors
m3.summary: Set one chart's up and/or down candle colors.
m3.hints: Hex colors; pass null for a side that should not change.

m3.name: volume.setState
m3.summary: Show, hide, or remove one chart's built-in Volume pane.
m3.hints: "hide volume" is hidden (stays in the legend); "remove volume" is removed (off the chart).

m3.name: chart.setSetting
m3.summary: Change one chart display setting from UCT's approved list (grid, crosshair, scale text, legend, watermark, labels, event/IPO markers, dark-pool levels, swing labels, prev-day lines, countdown, title, color mode, thin bars, inverted scale, gradient background, Volume pane look, Heikin Ashi, Chart IQ, position calculator, Info row / Bar info fields).
m3.hints: value = true/false for on/off settings (crosshair.mode, header.legendMode and bgMode too); a hex color (#2962ff) for colors; a number in range. Allowed — crosshair.mode, header.legendMode: always|hold|off; textSize: 8|10|11|12|14|16|18|20|22|24|28|32|40; header.titleMode: ticker|company|both; candleColorMode: onecolor|netchange|openclose; swingLabels.sensitivity: low|medium|high; crosshair.width, prevDayLevels.high|low|close.width, volume.maLineWidth: 1|2|3|4; crosshair.style, prevDayLevels.high|low|close.style, volume.maLineStyle: solid|dashed|dotted; watermark.sizeScale: 0.5|0.75|1|1.25|1.5|2|2.5|3|4; watermark.weight: 300|400|500|600|700|800; bgMode: solid|gradient; volume.barStyle: columns|histogram; volume.paneHeightPct: 8–45 (whole); volume.maPeriod: 0–500 (whole); watermark.opacity|x|y: 0–1; positionCalc.accountSize: 0–1000000000; positionCalc.riskPct: 0–100. header.fields|barInfo: +/-field ("+Market Cap"). Anything else: no op — say where it lives in Chart Settings.
m3.shape: args {"setting": <one id from the list>, "value": …} — "turn the gradient off" = {"setting":"bgMode","value":"solid"}, "gradient on" = {"setting":"bgMode","value":"gradient"}, "hide the grid" = {"setting":"grid.visible","value":false}. Never invent a setting id (no "bgGradient.enabled", no "background.gradient"): an on/off wish for a setting not listed is unsupported.

m3.name: chart.applyTemplate
m3.summary: Apply one of the member's saved chart templates to ONE chart, exactly as clicking it does (Chart Settings → Templates, or right-click → Chart template): the chart takes the template's whole saved setup, its indicators included.
m3.hints: template = a name from chartTemplates, exactly. For several charts ("all my charts"), one op per chart.

m3.name: chart.resetDefaults
m3.summary: Restore ONE chart's look to UCT's defaults (Chart Settings → Restore defaults): colours, markers, header, watermark and display settings. The chart's indicators are kept exactly as they are.
m3.hints: target = the chart. Always shown as a proposal first.

m3.name: chart.goToDate
m3.summary: Scroll ONE chart so a past date is at its right edge — exactly the Time Navigator date box. A view change only: every bar stays on the chart (it is not a replay), nothing is saved; Undo scrolls back.
m3.hints: date = YYYY-MM-DD. "As it looked on <date>" = this (say in the reply that later bars are still there, just scrolled off to the right).

m3.name: chart.compare
m3.summary: Overlay other symbols on ONE chart (Tools → Compare Symbols): add tickers, remove some, or clear all comparisons.
m3.hints: add = tickers to overlay, uppercase ([] for none); remove = tickers to take off ([] for none); clear = true to remove every comparison. "Compare NVDA against QQQ on this chart" = target the NVDA chart, add [QQQ].

m3.name: chart.addCustomTimeframe
m3.summary: Add a custom timeframe (e.g. 45 minutes, 2 hours, 3 days) to ONE chart's timeframe menu, exactly like the menu's Custom interval, and optionally switch the chart to it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.

fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema20: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 20-day exponential moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma50: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 50-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_sma200: Percent the price is above (+) or below (-) its 200-day simple moving average. [d]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema9: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 9-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.pct_vs_ema10: Percent the close is above (+) or below (-) its 10-day exponential moving average. [e]
fieldNotes.run_sma50_sma200: The 50-day SMA against the 200-day SMA: +1 is a golden cross, -1 a death cross. [f] [g] [h] [i] [j] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_10d: Mean daily volume of the last 10 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.avg_volume_50d: Mean daily volume of the last 50 sessions, the last one included. [m] [e]
fieldNotes.min_volume_3d_prior: The lowest daily volume of the three sessions before the last one (TC2000's MINV3.1). The last session is left out, so one heavy day cannot lift it. Blank if any of the three has no volume. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_trend_pct: Percent the 5-session average volume stands above (+) or below (-) the 20-session average, both ending at the last session. Blank if any of those sessions has no volume or the 20-session average is zero. [e]
fieldNotes.vol_up_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on more volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not rise. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.vol_down_run: Consecutive sessions, ending at the last one, each on less volume than the session before. 0 when the last session did not fall. [n] [e]
fieldNotes.new_high_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a high below the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close above the N-session high, the last session excluded, so 20 is a 20-day breakout. A close that only equals a prior high does not count. A short history can only count the sessions it holds. [e]
fieldNotes.new_low_lookback: How many consecutive prior sessions have a low above the last close, up to 252. At least N is a close below the N-session low, the last session excluded. [e]
fieldNotes.breakout_20d_age: Sessions since the latest close above the highest high of the 20 sessions before it. 0 is the last session. Blank when none happened in the last 63 sessions or with fewer than 21 sessions of history. [e]
fieldNotes.high_52w_age: Sessions since the highest high of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]
fieldNotes.low_52w_age: Sessions since the lowest low of the last 252 sessions was set. 0 is the last session. [o] [e]

fieldNotesKey.a: Before the open (4:00–9:30 ET) the change is against the prior close; after the close (to 8:00 PM ET) it is against today's close.
fieldNotesKey.b: Overnight and on weekends it shows the last after-hours trade; blank during the session.
fieldNotesKey.c: No extended-hours volume is available, so these screens cannot filter on it.
fieldNotesKey.d: During the session this follows the live price, while a field measured at the last completed session does not, so comparing the two mixes two clocks.
fieldNotesKey.e: Measured at the last completed session.
fieldNotesKey.f: Positive counts consecutive sessions above, negative consecutive sessions below, and 0 means level on the last session.
fieldNotesKey.g: +1 is the session it crossed up, -1 the session it crossed down, so a cross within N sessions that still holds is 1 to N (or -1 to -N).
fieldNotesKey.h: A cross that has since reversed no longer counts.
fieldNotesKey.i: Counted over the 400 stored sessions at most.
fieldNotesKey.k: Yes when the average stands above its own value 20 sessions earlier.
fieldNotesKey.m: Blank if any of them has no volume.
fieldNotesKey.n: A session with no volume ends the run.
fieldNotesKey.o: Blank without a full year, except a stock listed inside the year.

screener.compose: filters are ANDed. Field vs field: {field, op: gt_col|gte_col|lt_col|lte_col, other: a second number key} ("above the price target" = price gt_col pt_target). Candle Type: op contains, values = pattern words (every word must match); op in = any of them. OR / NOT: logic = a JSON STRING holding one tree of {"any":[…]}, {"all":[…]}, {"none":[…]} or {"not":x}, at most 4 deep; a leaf is one filter object, numbers in value/max as in filters; it is ANDed with filters. Up 5% today or 15% on the week: logic = "{\"any\":[{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1d\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":5},{\"field\":\"chg_pct_1w\",\"op\":\"gte\",\"value\":15}]}". rank = a JSON STRING of [{"field":…,"weight":…,"lower_better":true|false}], number fields, percentile-weighted within the screen, sets the order (sort_field null). lower_better is the member's, ask if unclear. Never replace an any / none / not with a nearby flat filter, and never drop a condition you cannot say. mode: a request with its own stocks and conditions that does not point at the earlier results is new, even right after a screen; never copy lastScreen filters into it.
